meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('necessary, needed').

переходить.gloss: to cross, to move on to

meanings.en: to cross, to move on to
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cross, to move on to', paired with 'перейти'.

examples.text: Он от слов переходит к делу.
examples.trans: He moves from words to action.

examples.text: Иван Васильевич от слов переходит к делу.
examples.trans: Ivan Vasilyevich is moving from words to action.

examples.text: Соколов переходит в вашу группу. Вот и договорились!
examples.trans: Sokolov is transferring to your group. Then it's settled!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ледующий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('next, following').

examples.text: А ты в следующий раз на мои деньги не рассчитывай. И всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Well, next time don't count on my money. And everything will be fine.

examples.text: А ты в следующий раз на мои деньги не рассчитывай.
examples.trans: Well, next time don't count on my money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ровень'). Common masculine noun meaning 'level' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'dessert' (from 'desservir', to clear the table).

examples.text: Гости в зале уже спрашивают новые десерты.
examples.trans: Guests in the dining room are already asking for new desserts.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: А ты иди на биржу труда. Там есть работа.
examples.trans: You go to the job centre. There's work there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'который'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('some, certain').

examples.trans: To some, life itself gives a chance.

examples.text: Некоторым сама жизнь даёт второй шанс.
examples.trans: To some, life itself gives a second chance.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

получаться.gloss: to work out, to come out

meanings.en: to work out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work out, to come out', paired with 'получиться'.

examples.text: Нет, не получается у меня это забыть. Удачи тебе на новом месте работы.
examples.trans: No, I just can't forget it. Good luck to you in your new job.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'labour, work' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The job centre is over there.

examples.text: А ты иди на биржу труда. Там есть работа.
examples.trans: You go to the job centre. There's work there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ладкий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sweet').

examples.text: Ты такой смешной, Тузик! Кто такой сладкий?
examples.trans: You're so funny, Tuzik! Who's so sweet?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'night' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'instead of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я буду мэром вместо него, чтобы его потом вытащить.
examples.trans: I'll be mayor instead of him, so I can get him out later.

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go (by vehicle), to set off
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle), to set off', paired with 'ехать'.

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

выпить.gloss: to drink (up); to have a drink

meanings.en: to drink (up); to have a drink
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drink (up); to have a drink', paired with 'пить'.

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

examples.trans: May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

examples.text: Милый, можно я выпью капельку пива?
examples.trans: Darling, may I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'coffee' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лететь'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fly, to start flying'.

examples.text: Я из-за тебя не полетела в Милан!
examples.trans: I missed the Milan trip because of you!
Tomorrow we will fly to rest, okay?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'довольствие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'pleasure' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Даже Лёша начал ходить в садик с удовольствием.
examples.trans: Even Lyosha started going to daycare with pleasure.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ожать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to adore, to love deeply'.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'what; what a', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'T-shirt' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here, put on this T-shirt right now.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть футболка.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always T-shirt.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be liked, to please', paired with 'понравиться'.

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'or', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

заниматься.gloss: to be busy with, to do

meanings.en: to be busy with, to do
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ниматься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be busy with, to do', paired with 'заняться'.
